destination: New self-serve workspaces are billed per active seat-hour through the new metering pipeline, and every invoice reconciles to the ledger within 0.5% before month-end close.
notes: Finance owns reconciliation rules. Legacy flat-rate customers stay on the old invoicer until a separate migration effort. One decision per working session; record the answer on the ticket and one line in Decisions so far.

decisions_so_far.gist: Meter on seat-hours aggregated hourly, not raw events.
Price in the billing provider; we send usage, they rate it.
Rename account_id to workspace_id with expand-migrate-contract before metering ships.

fog: How proration works when a workspace changes plan mid-cycle — depends on the provider's rating model (D2) and the dunning policy (D5).
Whether usage alerts go to the workspace owner or the billing contact.

out_of_scope.reason: Destination covers new self-serve workspaces only; legacy migration is its own effort.

tickets.title: Unit of metering
tickets.question: What unit do we meter and bill on?
tickets.resolution: Seat-hours aggregated hourly. Raw events are too noisy to explain on an invoice; daily seats under-bill bursty teams.

tickets.title: Where pricing logic lives
tickets.question: Do we rate usage ourselves or send usage to the billing provider to rate?
tickets.resolution: Provider rates usage. Its metered-price API covers seat-hours with tiers; in-house rating would duplicate tax and invoicing logic.

tickets.title: Identifier for billable entity
tickets.question: Which identifier keys usage records, given account_id is overloaded?
tickets.resolution: Rename to workspace_id using expand-migrate-contract so no caller breaks mid-way.

tickets.title: Invoice line presentation
tickets.question: How should seat-hour usage appear on the invoice so customers can check it?
options: One line per day with seat-hour totals

tickets.title: Dunning on failed usage invoices
tickets.question: What happens to a workspace when a usage invoice fails to collect?
options: Downgrade to free tier after 14 days

tickets.title: Sandbox account with provider
tickets.question: Can we obtain a provider sandbox with metered prices enabled so D4 can be prototyped against real invoices?

tickets.title: Add workspace_id alongside account_id
acceptance_criteria: Every usage-writing call accepts workspace_id and account_id and stores both
Existing test suite passes with no caller changes

tickets.title: Move admin and reporting callers to workspace_id
acceptance_criteria: No admin or reporting caller passes account_id

tickets.title: Remove account_id from usage records
acceptance_criteria: account_id column dropped from usage records
Search for account_id in usage code returns zero hits

tickets.title: One workspace's seat-hours appear as usage at the provider
tickets.demo: Activate two seats in a sandbox workspace for three hours; the provider dashboard shows 6 seat-hours.
acceptance_criteria: An hour with 2 active seats reports exactly 2 seat-hours
A retried aggregation run does not double-report usage
Failed provider calls are retried and logged with the workspace_id

tickets.title: Month-end reconciliation report for metered workspaces
tickets.demo: Finance opens the report for the sandbox month and sees each workspace's billed vs metered seat-hours with variance.
acceptance_criteria: Each workspace row shows metered, billed and variance percent
Rows with variance above 0.5% are highlighted
